sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was front-loaded: revenue more than doubled in FY2017 [F2][D36] and rose 64.2% in FY2021 [F6][D218], then stalled at 0.1% in FY2023 [F8][D311].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3.49 billion [F12] was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the IPO-related RSUs and the CEO award [P74].
The operating margin has improved from a -422.5% low in FY2017 [F22][D553] to -9.0% in FY2025 [F30][D554], a 5.7pp gain in the latest year alone [D419].
North America still supplies 58.6% of revenue in FY2025 [D456] but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D458][D406].
Other Revenue grew 62.9% and contributed 5.4pp, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp [D544][D545][D538].
Advertising rose on a roughly 17% increase in impressions, partly offset by a roughly 10% lower cost per impression, while other revenue grew on subscription subscriber growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth [D423][D406], an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025 [D425], so the 35.7% smaller EPS loss [D409] lagged the 34.0% smaller net loss [D408].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% [F30] sits well above the -32.4% window median [D555] and is the window high [D554].
Cost of revenue fell to 45.0% of revenue from 46.1% [D386][D338], adding 1.1pp to margin [D431], while R&D added 1.3pp [D432].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, plus $19.9 million of prior-year restructuring charges [P22].
R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount, partly offset by $38.8 million of prior-year restructuring charges [P23].
Net margin of -7.8% [F50] beat operating margin of -9.0% [F30], helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million [F80] was 11.1% of revenue [D394], well above the $460.5 million net loss [F40].
That gap is mostly non-cash: stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion and D&A of $163.6 million [P13].
Free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F100][D393], against a -4.1% window median [D561].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue [F90][D392] and 1.34x D&A [D395].
Net cash swung to -$596.3 million in FY2025 from $1.44 billion in FY2021 [D399][D211], a fourth straight year of decline [R3].
That -10.1% of revenue [D400] ranks at the 0th percentile against internet peers, whose median is 45.0% [D578][D579].
The company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of notes in February 2025 [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow [D401][D402], and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 [D390] and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2].
Net cash has fallen for four straight years into net debt [R3][D211][D399].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Whether the operating margin holds above the -9.0% FY2025 level [F30] or slips back toward the -32.4% median [D555], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether net cash recovers from -$596.3 million [D399] or extends the four-year decline [R3], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether stock-based compensation falls below the 17.1% of revenue seen in FY2025 [D390], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
